title: T-SMART: Mechanism-Level Attribution for Tool-Augmented Time-Series Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2609.14142v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can struggle with time-series question answering (TS-QA), especially when numerical signals are serialized as text and require explicit computation. Tool-augmented approaches improve performance, but existing systems often intertwine language reasoning, computation, and perception, making it difficult to determine which components drive the gains. We present T-SMART, a neurosymbolic framework that separates these roles: a frozen LLM interprets questions and selects operations, deterministic tools perform numerical computation, and structured perception is invoked only when needed. Controlled paired ablations show that deterministic computation provides the dominant benefit, improving accuracy by 31.7 percentage points over direct LLM reasoning on serialized time series, while language understanding and perception offer smaller complementary gains. translated_title: T-SMART：面向工具增强时间序列问答的机制级归因
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在时间序列问答（TS-QA）任务中可能表现不佳，尤其是当数值信号被序列化为文本且需要显式计算时。工具增强的方法能够提升性能，但现有系统往往将语言推理、计算和感知交织在一起，导致难以确定究竟是哪些组件带来了性能提升。我们提出了T-SMART，这是一个神经符号框架，将这些角色清晰分离：冻结的LLM负责解释问题并选择操作，确定性工具执行数值计算，结构化感知仅在需要时被调用。受控的成对消融实验表明，确定性计算提供了主要的收益，在序列化时间序列上相比直接LLM推理将准确率提升了31.7个百分点，而语言理解和感知则提供了较小的互补性增益。这些结果表明，工具增强的TS-QA的性能提升主要来自……
tldr: T-SMART是一个神经符号框架，通过将语言推理、确定性数值计算和结构化感知三种角色分离，并通过消融实验证明确定性计算是工具增强时间序列问答性能提升的主要来源，相比直接LLM推理可将准确率提高31.7个百分点。
en_tdlr: T-SMART is a neurosymbolic framework that disentangles language reasoning, deterministic numerical computation, and structured perception in tool-augmented time-series question answering, with controlled ablations showing that deterministic computation is the dominant source of gains, improving accuracy by 31.7 percentage points over direct LLM reasoning.
